#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --account=project_2001659
#   --partition=gputest
#   --ntasks=1
#   --cpus-per-task=40
#   --mem=0
#   --time=15
#   --gres=gpu:v100:4

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 40
#flux: --time-limit=15m

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:v100:4
# Flux GPU requests/type constraints are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without GPUs (or without V100s / fewer than 4), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm options: --account=project_2001659 and --partition=gputest
# Flux accounting/project selection and queue/partition selection are site-specific; no portable equivalents.
# Performance implication: job may be charged differently, have different priority/limits, run on different hardware, or be rejected.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=0
# Flux memory requests/limits are site/config dependent; no universally portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: if memory limits are enforced, the job may be constrained differently than intended.

module purge
module load pytorch

# Slurm used srun; under Flux, use flux-run.
# torchrun spawns 4 worker processes; run it as a single launcher task.
flux run -n 1 -c 40 torchrun --standalone --nnodes=1 --nproc_per_node=4 mnist_ddp.py --epochs=100

reasons: The original Slurm job required 4 V100 GPUs (`--gres=gpu:v100:4`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job specified an account and partition (`--account=project_2001659`, `--partition=gputest`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/account selection; on sites where these affect eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

The original Slurm job set `--mem=0` (unlimited memory on some Slurm systems) but the Flux resource section does not request/encode any memory policy; memory constraints may differ under Flux site configuration.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=project_2001659
#SBATCH --partition=gputest
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=40
#SBATCH --mem=0
#SBATCH --time=15
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:v100:4

module purge
module load pytorch

# Old way with torch.distributed.run
# srun python3 -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nnodes=1 --nproc_per_node=4 mnist_ddp.py --epochs=100

# New way with torchrun
srun torchrun --standalone --nnodes=1 --nproc_per_node=4 mnist_ddp.py --epochs=100
